title: Filename times give no clear common frequency drift in 26 selected Nancay sessions of FRB 20220912A
abstract: We test a common signed frequency slope within selected Nancay sessions of FRB 20220912A. We match all 696 public summary rows to candidate-filename times. The main sample has 581 groups in 26 sessions. The equal-session mean slope is +13.32 MHz/hour, with a nominal 95% session-bootstrap range of -51.50 to +65.98 and a two-sided within-session random-order probability of 0.61555. All planned controls remain uncertain. This test differs from prior absolute-gap and adjacent-similarity tests. It finds no new physical signal. A fixed-threshold score check has only about 48 percent sensitivity to a 50 MHz/hour common slope. Finite band response, detection selection, uncertain time conventions and the absence of raw-spectrum or independent-telescope tests limit physical claims. Code, aggregate results, input hashes, a figure and external-data retrieval steps are supplied.
